The cursor blinked relentlessly on her word processor screen, daring her to keep typing, as if somehow, magically, something worthwhile might yet emerge from this abyss.

Eventually, Lena got up and wandered out into the autumn sunlight. It was cool against her skin, but nothing seemed to change inside – every step she took felt like trudging through quicksand. Her gaze drifted down toward parked cars in the lot below, their shiny surfaces reflecting nothing of her inner turmoil.

Lena let herself get tangled in some nearby bushes, her face hidden as if trying to escape reality itself – there were, after all, so many easier things to worry about.
